**Explanation:** 
The pacing in the story is carefully controlled to reflect the monotony, stillness, and isolation of Ilse's environment and job. The initial ferry crossing unfolds nearly in "real-time," filled with small, quiet sensory details (the hum of the motor, the creaking of the rope, brief exchanges with passengers) that establish a slow, rhythmic pace matching the slow movement of the boat through the dense fog. 

On the return trip, when the ferry is empty, time is appropriately compressed into a few short paragraphs, as there are no interactions to anchor the scene, emphasizing how all the crossings blur together ("Der Nebel machte aus der Rückfahrt dieselbe Fahrt wie die Hinfahrt"). Finally, at the very end of the story, time is slightly stretched during the brief moment when her phone rings. Drawing out the few seconds of the phone vibrating while she stares at the name "Jonas" and the empty deck effectively creates emotional weight and quiet tension, shifting the focus to her internal world before she silences the call.
